record.original_question: For binary Reed–Muller codes, determine the weight enumerators of R_2(ν,m) in the unresolved range 3 ≤ ν ≤ m−4.

evidence.quote: It is an old problem to find the weight enumerators of R2(ν, m), 3 ≤ ν ≤ m − 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $m \ge 1$ and $0 \le 
u \le m$, the binary Reed–Muller code $R(
u,m)$ of order $
u$ and length $2^m$ is the linear code over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose codewords are the evaluation vectors $(f(x))_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^m}$ of all Boolean polynomials $f \in \mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ of total degree at most $
u$. The weight enumerator of a binary linear code $C$ of length $n$ is the polynomial
$$W_C(X,Y) \;=\; \sum_{c \in C} X^{n - \mathrm{wt}(c)} Y^{\mathrm{wt}(c)} \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{n} A_i\, X^{n-i} Y^i,$$
where $\mathrm{wt}(c)$ is the Hamming weight of $c$ and $A_i = \#\{c \in C : \mathrm{wt}(c) = i\}$.

Determine, for every pair of integers $(
u, m)$ with $3 \le 
u \le m-4$, the weight enumerator of the binary Reed–Muller code $R(
u,m)$; equivalently, give a closed-form expression (or explicit formula) for the weight distribution $\{A_i : 0 \le i \le 2^m\}$ of $R(
u,m)$ in this range of parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the weight enumerators of binary Reed–Muller codes $R(\nu,m)$ in the range $3 \le \nu \le m-4$ is a long-standing open problem. Exact weight distributions have been obtained only in isolated low-dimensional cases (e.g., third-order Reed–Muller codes of lengths 512 and 1024 via classification of cubic Boolean forms, and recent work on $R(4,9)$), while general formulas remain unknown. Recent surveys and sampling/estimation papers (2020–2025) explicitly treat the problem as still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Reed-Muller Codes: Theory and Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Reed-Muller codes noting that exact weight distributions are known only in very limited orders.
status_evidence.claim: General weight distribution of Reed-Muller codes remains unresolved beyond limited cases.

status_evidence.title: Estimating the Weight Enumerators of Reed-Muller Codes via Sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes sampling-based estimation because exact computation is infeasible for general parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Exact weight enumerators for general R(r,m) are not known; estimation is needed.

status_evidence.title: The weight distribution of the fourth-order Reed–Muller code of length 512
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the weight distribution of R(4,9), a previously open case.
status_evidence.claim: Only isolated new cases have been resolved; the general problem persists.
